chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The loud laugh (qahqahah) does not break the ablution, but it breaks the prayer.
ai.seo_question: Does loud laughter break wudu or only salat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential distinction between the nullification of prayer and the breaking of ablution, establishing that loud laughter (qahqahah) breaks the prayer but not the wudu. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it differentiates between acts that require immediate continuation of prayer versus those requiring a fresh state of purity, reflecting the Imams' precise categorization of ritual invalidators. The chain of transmission through Zurarah and Jamil ibn Darraj highlights the reliability of this legal nuance within the Usuli tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The chuckling (laughing) does not break the ablution, and (but) it breaks the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Laughing does not invalidate Wudu’ but it invalidates Salah (prayer).”’
